name: TigerGraph
tagline: Distributed MPP graph database built for deep-link analytics on very large graphs.
description: TigerGraph is a native, massively parallel graph database written in C++ that shards a single graph across a cluster and runs queries in parallel on every partition. Its GSQL language compiles procedural, accumulator-based queries, which makes 10-hop traversals and whole-graph analytics practical on billions of edges; recent 4.x releases add openCypher and GQL-style pattern matching plus TigerVector for vector search inside graph queries. It suits enterprises with large, fast-changing graphs (fraud, supply chain, customer 360). Expect a steeper learning curve than Cypher-first databases and a mostly commercial licensing model.

pricing.notes: Free Community Edition for limited data sizes; TigerGraph Savanna cloud is usage-based; Enterprise licensed by contract.

scale.notes: Automatic partitioning of one graph across nodes with replication; cross-region replication for DR.

strengths: Shards a single graph across nodes and runs every query hop in parallel (MPP)
GSQL accumulators make multi-hop analytics and custom algorithms expressible in one query
Handles deep-link queries (10+ hops) on billions of edges with interactive latency
TigerVector lets vector similarity and graph traversal run in the same query
Real-time updates coexist with analytics, avoiding a separate graph OLAP copy
weaknesses: GSQL is proprietary and has a steep learning curve compared with Cypher
Strict schema and installed-query workflow slow down ad-hoc exploration
Closed source; the free edition is size-limited and community is smaller than Neo4j's
Cluster sizing and memory planning are non-trivial for self-managed deployments
notIdealFor: Small graphs where an embedded or single-node DB suffices
Teams wanting a fully open-source stack
